Summary and policy lens
- FOMC kept the target range at 2.25–2.50% and signaled patience, citing slower household/business spending and muted inflation with low market-based inflation compensation.
- January 2019 SLOOS corroborates downside/credit headwinds: banks tightened standards for C&I loans and construction/land development, reported wider loan rate spreads in some segments, and saw weaker demand for business credit, residential real estate loans, and HELOCs. Banks also expected tighter standards and weaker demand through 2019, with concerns about deteriorating performance in mortgages and nonprime consumer credit. While some categories remained unchanged and earlier easing was noted for large firms/loan covenants, the net SLOOS signal is tightening and softer demand.
- Implication: Tighter bank credit and softer loan demand reinforce the case for a pause to avoid amplifying financial accelerator dynamics. This tilts the assessment more dovish than a purely macro read of low inflation and solid labor markets alone.

Net tone: dovish with credit-headwind and financial-stability awareness.
